study_name.notes: Study protocol registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02217384) but no canonical study name identifier provided.

target_condition.evidence_quote: Anorexia nervosa (AN) is an eating disorder with a high mortality.

country.evidence_quote: only included Danish Caucasian women with AN cases, recruited from three specialized centres in Denmark

location.value: Odense University Hospital, Aarhus University Hospital, Aalborg University Hospital
location.evidence_quote: Center for Eating Disorders (Odense University Hospital), Child and Adolescent Psychiatric Unit (Aarhus University Hospital) and Unit for Psychiatric Research (Aalborg University Hospital)

body_site.evidence_quote: faecal and serum samples, respectively, from a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females

sequencing_platform.evidence_quote: Purified and amplified DNA fragment libraries were sequenced using the Ion Proton Sequencer (Thermo Fisher)

dna_extraction_kit.notes: Paper states 'DNA extraction from aliquots of faecal samples was performed following IHMS SOP P7 V2' but does not name a specific extraction kit.

sex.evidence_quote: we decided to include only women in the present study

antibiotics_exclusion_period.evidence_quote: antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months

westernized.notes: Inferred as westernized based on recruitment from Denmark (high-income country)

age.notes: Individual participant ages not reported; study includes 'age-matched' controls but specific age values not provided in tables or text

subject_id.notes: Individual subject identifiers not provided in manuscript or supplementary tables

sample_id.notes: Individual sample identifiers not provided in manuscript

control.notes: Study compares AN cases (n=77) and healthy controls (n=70) but individual sample-level case/control assignment not provided

ncbi_accession.notes: NCBI SRA/ENA accessions not mentioned in manuscript or supplementary materials

age_min.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_min.notes: EDI-3 age range; paper does not explicitly state the exact ages of included participants, only that they were Danish Caucasian women recruited from specialized centres.

age_max.evidence_quote: EDI-3 developed from current theories related to pathogenesis and diagnosis of eating disorders and it was designed for use in females aged 13–53 years.
age_max.notes: EDI-3 design age range; actual participant ages not explicitly specified in methods.

antibiotics_current_use.evidence_quote: Exclusion criteria comprised antibiotic or antifungal treatment within the previous 3 months
antibiotics_current_use.notes: Exclusion criterion for both AN patients and healthy controls; antibiotic use within 3 months prior was exclusionary.

bmi.evidence_quote: women with AN were much leaner; the exclusion criteria for the age-matched healthy control women were BMI below 18.5 or above 25 kg m −2
bmi.notes: HC BMI range is explicit (18.5–25 kg/m²). AN BMI described qualitatively as 'much leaner' but Supplementary Table 1 not provided in text. Mouse FMT donors: AN females aged 20, 22, 20 with BMI 10.3, 11.5, 11.7; HC females aged 20, 22, 21 with BMI 22.6, 21.1, 21.2.

disease.evidence_quote: The AN patients were all diagnosed by an experienced consultant psychiatrist and they met the DSM-5 criteria for the restricting or binge/purging subtypes of AN.
disease.notes: AN cases diagnosed using DSM-5 criteria; HC were healthy-weight volunteers without eating disorders.

disease_details.evidence_quote: It can be classified into two subtypes, the common restricting (AN-RS) type and the less prevalent binge-eating or purging (AN-BP) type
disease_details.notes: Two DSM-5 subtypes included in study; AN-RS n=56, AN-BP n=21.

obgyn_birth_control.evidence_quote: regular medication of any kind apart from birth control pills
obgyn_birth_control.notes: Birth control pills were explicitly excluded from 'regular medication' restrictions for healthy controls, implying some participants may have been using them, but current use is not explicitly stated.

smoker.notes: Smoking status was used as a covariate in analyses but prevalence/status of individual participants not reported in text.

treatment.evidence_quote: All the below-described measurements were conducted during routine treatment in the specialized unit; Individually customized meals were given under the supervision of trained nurses or dietitians
treatment.notes: Medications (SSRIs, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines) were adjusted for in analyses. Treatment details differ between in-patient and out-patient cohorts.

fmt_role.evidence_quote: we transplanted faecal microbiota from three randomly chosen AN-RS cases and three age-matched HC participants to three independent litters of female germ-free (GF) mice
fmt_role.section: Results — Gut microbiota induces reduced weight gain
fmt_role.notes: FMT study used 3 AN-RS donors and 3 HC donors; recipients were female germ-free mice, n=8, 6, 6 per litter (total AN-T n=10, HC-T n=10 examined over 3 independent experiments).

biomarker_name.evidence_quote: Multiple bacterial taxa (for example, Clostridium species) were altered in AN and correlated with estimates of eating behaviour and mental health.
biomarker_name.notes: Comprehensive list of biomarkers identified throughout the study as altered in AN cases versus healthy controls, including bacterial species, metabolites, and serum markers.

biomarker_unit.evidence_quote: Serum metabolomics revealed an increase in metabolites associated with reduced food intake (for example, indole-3-propionic acid).
biomarker_unit.notes: Biomarkers were measured using various units including relative abundance, serum concentration, absolute abundance, and gene expression levels.

value: positively correlated with eating disorder scores
inversely correlated with eating disorder scores
biomarker_value.evidence_quote: Among the depleted species in AN were Roseburia intestinalis and Roseburia inulinivorans, species that have a high capacity for digesting plant polysaccharides and are considered to be part of the health-related gut microbiota.
biomarker_value.section: Results — Gut microbiota composition is altered in AN
biomarker_value.notes: Biomarker values indicate directional changes (increased/decreased/altered) and associations with AN phenotypes.

disease_response_os.notes: Overall survival data not reported in this study; the study is a cross-sectional microbiome and metabolomics analysis, not a survival trial.

ecog_performance_status.notes: ECOG performance status not reported; study focuses on microbiome and metabolome in AN patients, not performance status assessment.

value: higher β-diversity at genus level in AN
higher β-diversity at species level in AN
reduced bacterial cell counts not significantly different between AN and HC
reduced Bacteroidota and Actinobacteriota at phylum level in AN
reduction in viral–bacterial interactions in AN (219 in HC versus 84 in AN)
enrichment of Lactococcus phages in AN
altered bacterial growth rates in AN
increased structural variants in bacterial genomes in AN
feces_phenotype_value.evidence_quote: Comparing stool samples from AN and HC, there was no significant difference in bacterial cell counts between AN and HC or within subtypes of AN.
feces_phenotype_value.section: Results — Phenotypes of women with AN and controls
feces_phenotype_value.notes: Fecal microbiota phenotypes characterized through metagenomics, viromics, and metabolomics analyses.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: Tumor size not applicable; this is a microbiome study of anorexia nervosa, not an oncology study.

tumor_size_residual_measurement.notes: Residual tumor size not applicable; this is not a cancer treatment study.

value: Study cohort: 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females (age-matched)
Study design: Cross-sectional with faecal microbiota transplantation in mice
AN subtypes: restricting (AN-RS, n=56) and binge/purging (AN-BP, n=21)
Sample collection: Shotgun metagenomics on faecal samples; untargeted metabolomics on serum
Sequencing depth: Minimum 20 million high-quality reads of 150 bp per library
Germ-free mice FMT: Faecal microbiota from 3 AN cases and 3 HC donors transplanted to female germ-free littermates
Caloric restriction in mice: 30% energy-restricted diet for 3 weeks
EDI-3 questionnaire used to assess eating disorder symptoms
Covariates adjusted: age, BMI, smoking, multiple drug intake
Statistical significance: P_adj < 0.05 by Benjamini-Hochberg method
Bidirectional mediation analysis used to infer causal relationships
No antibiotics or antifungal treatment within 3 months prior to enrollment
Inclusion criterion for AN: DSM-5 criteria for restricting or binge/purging subtypes
uncurated_metadata.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples, respectively, from a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females.
uncurated_metadata.notes: Comprehensive study design and methodological metadata extracted from Abstract and Methods sections.

host_species.evidence_quote: Shotgun metagenomics and metabolomics were performed on faecal and serum samples, respectively, from a cohort of 77 females with AN and 70 healthy females. Further, we performed faecal microbiota transplantation from AN cases to germ-free mice under energy-restricted feeding.
host_species.notes: Study includes both human participants (females) and female germ-free mice (Swiss Webster strain) as study subjects.

extraction_warnings: Paper reports cohort-level data (77 AN cases, 70 healthy controls) without providing individual participant identifiers or per-sample metadata rows. Cannot populate sample_level granularity with individual rows as requested; data is aggregated at study level.
Supplementary Table 1 references clinical characteristics of enrolled women but actual table with per-participant data not provided in the text extract.
Individual participant ages not explicitly stated; only noted that controls were 'age-matched' to AN cases.
Study includes both inpatient and outpatient AN cases but sample-level assignment (in-patient vs out-patient status per sample) not available.
Mouse FMT experiments used 3 AN donors and 3 HC donors, but human donor sample identifiers and detailed metadata not provided.
Antibiotic exclusion period applies to both AN cases and HC controls per inclusion criteria, but not stratified by individual sample.
The paper registration at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT02217384) may contain additional per-participant metadata not reproduced in the published manuscript.
Batch 1 returned granularity='subgroup_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

Batch 1 subgroups ['Anorexia Nervosa (AN)', 'Healthy Controls (HC)', 'AN-RS (Restrictive Subtype)', 'AN-BP (Binge-Eating/Purging Subtype)', 'FMT Recipients - AN Donor (AN-T)', 'FMT Recipients - HC Donor (HC-T)'] differ from batch 0 []; kept batch 0.
Age information: The paper does not report exact participant ages, only the EDI-3 design range (13–53 years). Specific ages mentioned only for FMT donors (20, 22, 20 for AN; 20, 22, 21 for HC).

BMI subgroup values: Specific BMI values for human AN cohort are referenced as 'Supplementary Table 1' but the table itself is not provided in the text. For HC, BMI range is 18.5–25 kg/m². FMT donors' BMIs are reported in Methods.
Smoking status: Smoking was a covariate in analyses but individual smoking status/prevalence not explicitly reported.

Sample size discrepancy for FMT mice: Paper states 'AN-T n = 10, HC-T, n = 10, examined over 3 independent experiments' but also mentions '8, 6 and 6 littermates, respectively, were randomly assigned' (totaling 20 mice, not 10 per group); this may reflect pooling or re-analysis.
Medication use: Specific medications (SSRIs, antipsychotics, benzodiazepines) were noted as covariates; details on individual participant medication status not provided in main text.

Treatment details: In-patient meal protocols specify energy intake individualized per patient, with macronutrient composition 40–50% carbohydrate, 30–40% fat, 20–25% protein; specific individual intake values not reported.
Batch 2 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.
Study is not a clinical trial with individual patient outcomes; granularity is study_level, not sample_level.
No tumor-related or ECOG performance status data applicable to this microbiome study.
Overall survival data not reported; study is observational/cross-sectional with mechanistic mouse FMT experiments.
Biomarker values are reported at cohort/group level (AN vs. HC) with statistical comparisons, not individual patient values.

Biomarker units vary widely (relative abundance, serum concentration, gene expression, etc.); specific numerical values reported in figures and supplementary tables but aggregated here as directional changes.
